name: virel
author: toys-and-building agent
description: Toy block wall. Clue: `<digits>/<N>`, digits 2-6 = the brick widths of the BOTTOM course (left to right, 3-6 bricks, total width W in 12..26), N in 1..min(10,max(3,W//2-2)). Solution: an ASCII wall, one line per course, top course first, every course a gapless tiling of the same width W by bricks drawn `[`+`-`*(w-2)+`]` with w in 2..6 (`[]`,`[-]`,`[--]`,`[---]`,`[----]`). Three clauses, all verified from the clue: (1) at least 5 courses; (2) the LAST line is exactly the clue's brick widths; (3) exactly N *twin stacks* -- a twin stack is a brick that sits exactly on top of a brick with the same span (same left AND right edge) in the course below; counted over all adjacent course pairs. PRIVATE discovery path: one demo shows a block wall and 'the digits are the bottom row' is immediate; the whole difficulty is what N counts. Rivals the generator deliberately falsifies in every shipped demo (rejection filter in solve): number of courses, junctions, total bricks, aligned joints, same-width-above pairs, near-twins (same width, different span), width-2 bricks -- none of them ever equals N, and every wall carries >=2 stray aligned joints and >=2 near-twins so 'the joints line up' and 'same size above' are visibly wrong. Degenerate witnesses closed (measured, 300-400 fresh clues): empty/junk/clue-as-answer 0%; 1-4 course walls 0% (>=5 courses); the clue course repeated 2,3,4,5,6,9 times 0% (N<=10 makes k*(H-1) unreachable); a wall built to have zero twins 0%; a random valid wall 10-12%; best rival family (build a wall with aligned-joint count 2N / 2N+1) 18-23%; one fixed wall for all clues 0.2%; upside-down wall 0.2%. N frequently exceeds the number of bricks in the bottom course, so twins cannot all be placed at one junction. solve() randomises height 5-9, brick widths, which junctions carry the twins and all filler, and never emits the minimal witness.
